blocks.body: Hydro jetting clears a sewer line with a high-pressure water stream, fed through the same cleanout access point used for rodding. A specialized nozzle sprays water in every direction as it moves through the pipe, scouring grease, scale, and roots off the entire pipe wall instead of just cutting a path through the middle. It's the fix for buildup that keeps coming back after rodding, or for roots that have worked into the pipe joints. Rodding opens the line back up. Hydro jetting cleans it.

blocks.h2: Jetting Old Cast Iron Kitchen Lines
blocks.body: In many 1950s Skokie homes, the kitchen drain is cast iron. Over decades, the inside rusts and roughens, and grease sticks to that rough surface. A cable can poke through, but the line closes up again. Jetting removes the grease and loose scale, opening the pipe back up. If the pipe is too thin or cracked, we'll show you on camera and talk about replacement.

blocks.h2: Hydro Jetting Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: Will hydro jetting break my old clay sewer?
items.preview: Not if the pipe is sound. We check first.
items.answer: Not if it's sound. We camera the line first and set the pressure for its condition. If a section is already broken, we'll recommend a [repair](/skokie/sewer-repair) first.

items.q: Is jetting better than rodding for roots?
items.answer: Yes, for heavy roots. Rodding cuts a channel. Jetting removes the growth from the whole pipe wall, so it takes longer to return.

items.q: Can jetting clear an old cast iron kitchen line?
items.answer: Yes. Jetting removes grease and scale from cast iron lines and restores flow.

items.q: How often should a jetted line be checked?
items.preview: Every year or two if roots were the problem.
items.answer: If roots were the cause, a camera check every year or two catches regrowth early.

items.q: Does jetting work on a basement floor drain?
items.answer: Yes. It clears built-up sludge that rodding leaves behind.

items.q: How much does hydro jetting cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on the line and buildup. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the line length, access and how heavy the buildup is. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
